items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I never listened to anything but his Bud Powell roots which is where Bill Evans really came out of anyway.

ctx.x: For instance, the first time I heard — I was a senior in high school in Germany and I went down to the PX and bought this record Bill Evans “Sunday Live at the Village Vanguard.” I brought that back home, Scott LaFaro, Paul Motian. Put it on, now Bill Evans for me was this guy who used to play with Miles back in the late fifties and he’s on a couple of Miles’ records and so and I remember he also used to play with people like Jimmy Giuffre, Tony Scott, there were some — I remember that. But I never had any of…

like what I did a clinic on today. It’s rooted in the melodies and the rhythms, but the rhythms are not supposed to be as hard and fast and they’re not supposed to be as repetitive as some of the other kinds of traditional kinds of music are. And when you finally begin to understand the emotional depth as well as the difference in approach for articulation, the difference in approach for harmonic development, the difference of approach in terms of how you block out your phrases, the kind of phrasing that you use…
